feedback.problem:
Use the Laplace transform of $f(t)={e}^{kt}$ to find the Laplace transform of $\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5t).$$\,L{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5t)}=$ {{field-1}},
defined for {{field-2}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
The linearity property of the Laplace transform states that for functions $f(t)$ and $g(t),$ we have

$$
L{\alpha f(t)+\beta g(t)}=\alpha \cdot L{f(t)}+\beta \cdot L{g(t)},
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants.

First, recall that, by definition

$$
\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5t)=\frac{{e}^{5t}-{e}^{-5t}}{2}.
$$

Taking the Laplace transform and applying the linearity property, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5t)} & =L{\frac{{e}^{5t}-{e}^{-5t}}{2}} \\  & =L{\frac{{e}^{5t}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{-5t}}{2}} \\  & =L{\frac{{e}^{5t}}{2}}-L{\frac{{e}^{-5t}}{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}L{{e}^{5t}}-\frac{1}{2}L{{e}^{-5t}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we recall that 

$$
L{{e}^{kt}}=\frac{1}{s-k},\,s>k.
$$

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{5t}} & =\frac{1}{s-5},\,s>5 \\ L{{e}^{-5t}} & =\frac{1}{s+5},\,s>-5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Laplace transform of $\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5t)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5t)} & =\frac{1}{2}L{{e}^{5t}}-\frac{1}{2}L{{e}^{-5t}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{s-5}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{s+5} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{s-5}-\frac{1}{s+5}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{(s+5)-(s-5)}{(s-5)(s+5)}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{10}{{s}^{2}-25}) \\  & =\frac{5}{{s}^{2}-25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $L{{e}^{5t}}$ is defined for $s\in (5,\infty )$ and $L{{e}^{-5t}}$ is defined for $s\in (-5,\infty ),$ we have that $L{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5t)}$ is defined for

$$
(5,\infty )\cap (-5,\infty )=(5,\infty ),
$$

that is, $s>5.$
